title: Bohemia by Car — Spa Colonnades, Ore Mountains and Sandstone
subRegion: West Bohemia, Krušné hory and the Elbe sandstone

bestPeriod.note: The Krušné hory ridge road is snow-cleared but slow from November to March; the sandstone gorge boats run April to October only.

basecamps: Karlovy Vary, Mezní Louka and Kutná Hora
summary: A 950 km Bohemian loop from Prague through the spa triangle, along the Ore Mountains ridge and into the sandstone gorges of Bohemian Switzerland.
hook: Czechia does not do alpine passes, so this drive earns its scenery a different way: forest ridges at a thousand metres, spa towns built to be walked in, and a sandstone canyon where the road simply stops at the German border. The legs are short, the second-class roads are free, and the car is the point only about half the time.

snapshot.Base(s): Karlovy Vary (3 nights), Mezní Louka / Hřensko (2), Kutná Hora (1)
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: approx. 950 km; motorway D6/D8 plus long ridge and forest roads, max altitude approx. 1,100 m
snapshot.Getting There: Fly to Prague (PRG); collect the car at the airport, never in the centre
snapshot.Who It Suits: Slow drivers who want castles, colonnades and one serious gorge walk

itinerary.title: Out of Prague, west to the Ohře
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at Václav Havel Airport. Confirm the e-vignette is registered to the plate — Czechia has had no windscreen sticker since 2021 — and that dipped headlights come on automatically, because they are compulsory day and night, year round.
itinerary.afternoon: Take the D6 west, then drop south to **Křivoklát**, a royal hunting castle in the Berounka woods. The village car park is below the walls; the last 300 m is on foot. Rejoin the D6 for Karlovy Vary.
itinerary.evening: Detour to **Loket**, a granite spur town wrapped in a river meander, with a 12th-century castle above the square. Then 15 km on to Karlovy Vary. Park in a garage below the spa zone — the Lázeňská zóna is permit-only for cars and the enforcement is camera-based.
itinerary.dayStats: 175 km · 2h40 driving · no passes · max altitude 430 m.

itinerary.title: Karlovy Vary on foot, Bečov by car
itinerary.morning: Leave the car. Walk the Mlýnská, Tržní and Sadová colonnades, buy a porcelain **lázeňský pohárek** cup from a kiosk, and taste the springs in ascending temperature — Vřídlo, the geyser spring, runs at 73°C and is drunk cooled.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive 25 km south to **Bečov nad Teplou** for the Reliquary of St. Maur, the Romanesque shrine found under the castle chapel floor in 1985. Entry is by timed guided tour only and small groups sell out; book online the day before.
itinerary.evening: Back in Karlovy Vary, walk up to the Diana lookout tower by funicular and down through the forest path.
itinerary.dayStats: 60 km · 1h10 driving · no passes · max altitude 620 m.

itinerary.title: The spa triangle
itinerary.morning: West on the R6/D6 to **Cheb**, whose Špalíček merchant houses lean into the square, then 6 km to **Františkovy Lázně** — the smallest and flattest of the three UNESCO-listed Great Spas of Europe here, laid out in yellow neoclassical terraces.
itinerary.afternoon: South on the 21 and 230 to **Mariánské Lázně**: the cast-iron colonnade, the singing fountain on the hour, and forest roads through the Slavkovský les on the way back.
itinerary.evening: Return to Karlovy Vary on the 20/6. Third night in the same bed, which is the whole reason to base here.
itinerary.dayStats: 165 km · 2h50 driving · no passes · max altitude 780 m.

itinerary.title: The Ore Mountains ridge
itinerary.morning: Climb the hairpins of the 25 to **Jáchymov**, the silver and uranium town that gave the word "dollar" its root, then on to **Boží Dar** at 1,028 m — the highest town in Central Europe. The spur road to the **Klínovec** car park (1,244 m summit) tops out around 1,100 m; the last stretch is on foot or by chairlift.
itinerary.afternoon: Take the ridge road east — the 219 and 254 through Loučná pod Klínovcem, Hora Svaté Kateřiny and Nová Ves v Horách. This is the finest driving of the week: long open moorland curves at 800–900 m with the Bohemian basin dropping away to the south. Descend the switchbacks to Litvínov, then the D8 to Ústí nad Labem and Děčín.
itinerary.evening: Follow the Labe (Elbe) gorge road to **Hřensko**, the lowest point in Czechia at 115 m, and sleep at Mezní Louka. Parking in Hřensko itself is cramped, paid and slow; the Mezní Louka lot is bigger.
itinerary.dayStats: 210 km · 4h00 driving · 3 ridge saddles (Boží Dar, Hora Svaté Kateřiny, Nová Ves) · max altitude approx. 1,100 m.

itinerary.title: Bohemian Switzerland
itinerary.morning: Walk from Mezní Louka to **Pravčická brána**, Europe's largest sandstone arch, on the red-marked trail — about 3 km each way, entry approx. CZK 200 (€8). The Czech waymarking is a coloured stripe between two white ones and the network is dense; follow colours, not compass.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive down to Hřensko and take the punts through the **Edmundova soutěska** and **Divoká soutěska** gorges of the Kamenice. Ferrymen pole the boats between walls 50 m high; tickets are sold at the landing stage and the last departure is mid-afternoon.
itinerary.evening: Optional cross-border run to Bad Schandau and the **Bastei** bridge in Saxon Switzerland — 25 km, no border formalities, no German car toll.
itinerary.dayStats: 55 km · 1h10 driving · no passes · max altitude 415 m.

itinerary.title: Down the Labe to the silver town
itinerary.morning: Retrace the gorge to Děčín, then follow the river to **Litoměřice** for its arcaded square and the Chalice house, and stop at **Terezín**, the fortress town used as a ghetto and transit camp. Allow two unhurried hours; parking is free outside the Small Fortress.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue via **Mělník**, where the Vltava meets the Labe below a castle terrace planted with Ludmila vines, then cross-country on the 16 and 38 to Kutná Hora.
itinerary.evening: Walk the Barborská terrace above the Jesuit college at dusk, after the coaches leave.
itinerary.dayStats: 205 km · 3h20 driving · no passes · max altitude 380 m.

itinerary.title: Kutná Hora and back to Prague
itinerary.morning: The **Sedlec Ossuary** opens early and issues timed tickets; take the first slot and combine it with the cathedral of the Assumption next door. Then the cathedral of **St. Barbara**, a late-Gothic hall church funded by silver miners.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive the 111 and 125 through the Sázava woods to **Český Šternberk**, a castle on a rock spine still held by the family that built it in 1241. Guided tours in Czech with printed English text.
itinerary.evening: D1 into Prague and drop the car at the airport or a peripheral depot. Do not drive into Prague 1 with luggage; the tram is faster.
itinerary.dayStats: 100 km · 1h50 driving · no passes · max altitude 460 m.

accommodationStrategy.name: Grandhotel Pupp
accommodationStrategy.description: The anchor of the town since the 18th century, at the top of the pedestrian spa street with its own garage — which solves Karlovy Vary's real problem, that the centre is closed to unpermitted cars. Three nights here means three days without repacking.
accommodationStrategy.booking: two months ahead; longer for film-festival week in early July.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Mezní Louka
accommodationStrategy.description: A 19th-century hunting lodge at the trailhead for Pravčická brána, with a large open car park and a kitchen that serves late enough for walkers coming off the gorge trails. Staying here rather than in Hřensko avoids the morning parking scrum in the gorge village.
accommodationStrategy.booking: six weeks for weekends in high summer.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Mědínek Old Town
accommodationStrategy.description: On Palackého náměstí, three minutes from St. Barbara's and with parking behind the building — useful because Kutná Hora's old-town streets are narrow, one-way and heavily signed. Good position for the early ossuary slot.

logistics.emergency: 112 pan-European; 155 ambulance, 158 police, 150 fire. Mountain rescue (Horská služba) is **1210** and covers the Krušné hory and the sandstone parks.
logistics.money: Koruna, not euro. Cards work almost everywhere, but gorge boats, small car parks and village pubs are cash-first. Refuse dynamic currency conversion at ATMs.

other.label: E-vignette
other.text: Motorway and expressway use (D-class roads: D6, D8, D1, D11) requires a plate-linked electronic vignette bought at edalnicnizname.cz or the app — approx. CZK 300 (€12) for 10 days, CZK 480 (€19) for 30 days, CZK 2,570 (€105) annual. There is no sticker and no physical proof. First-class roads numbered 6, 13, 20 and so on are free, and several exempt sections are signposted.

other.label: Rental cars
other.text: Czech rentals normally include the vignette; check the plate on your confirmation. Cross-border into Germany, Austria, Poland and Slovakia is standard; the Balkans are usually excluded or surcharged €30–€60. One-way drops to Dresden or Vienna start around €150.

other.label: Germany's Umweltplakette
other.text: The Bastei detour needs nothing — neither Dresden nor Saxon Switzerland has a low-emission zone. If you extend to Leipzig, Halle or Berlin you need a green Umweltplakette on the windscreen, sold for €6–€20 at TÜV/DEKRA stations; rentals registered in Germany usually already carry one, Czech-plated cars usually do not.

other.label: Driving rules that are actually enforced
other.text: Dipped headlights 24/7 all year. Blood alcohol limit is zero — no glass of wine at lunch. Winter tyres are compulsory from 1 November to 31 March whenever there is snow, ice or slush. Speed cameras and section control are common on the D8 and around Ústí.

other.label: Emergencies
other.text: 112 pan-European; 155 ambulance, 158 police, 150 fire. Mountain rescue (Horská služba) is **1210** and covers the Krušné hory and the sandstone parks.

other.label: Opening-hour traps
other.text: Czech castles close entirely from November to March and run weekends-only in April and October; most shut on Mondays even in season. Guided tours are the only way in and the last tour is often 90 minutes before closing.

proTips: Book the Bečov reliquary tour and the St. Barbara / Sedlec combined ticket online the previous evening. Both cap group sizes and both sell out by mid-morning in summer.
Drive the Krušné hory ridge west to east. Eastbound, the Bohemian basin is on your right all afternoon and the light stays behind you.
At Hřensko, park at Mezní Louka and walk down to the gorge boats rather than driving in. The village road is a single lane between rock and river, and it gridlocks by 10:00.
Buy the spa cup, not bottled water: the Karlovy Vary springs are free, and the porcelain spout is designed to cool 73°C water on the way to your mouth.
Fill up in Czechia before crossing to Saxony. Czech fuel is consistently cheaper, and the border stations at Hřensko know it.
If rain kills the sandstone day, swap in Děčín castle's rose garden and the Ústí funicular to Větruše — both are ten minutes away and mostly indoors.

packingNotes: Grippy shoes with an edge: the sandstone steps at Pravčická brána stay damp and greasy even in August.
A light waterproof — the Elbe gorge makes its own weather.
Cash in koruna, roughly CZK 3,000, for boats, car parks and rural pubs.
Swimwear for a spa afternoon in Karlovy Vary or Mariánské Lázně.
A phone holder and offline maps; the ridge road loses signal in the border forests.
Something warm: Boží Dar sits at 1,028 m and runs 8–10°C below Prague.
whatCouldGoWrong: **Forest-fire or storm closure in Bohemian Switzerland.** Sections of the park have been closed for restoration since the 2022 fire and trails change year to year. Fallback: the Tisá rock town and the Děčínský Sněžník plateau, both 30 minutes away and unaffected.

**You drove a D-road without a vignette.** Fines are issued to the plate and follow the rental company back to you with an admin fee. Fallback: buy the vignette on your phone before you touch a D-road — activation is immediate.
**Castle shut on a Monday.** It will be. Fallback: build Mondays around towns, not castles — Kutná Hora, Litoměřice and Loket all work as walking days.
**Prague airport drop at rush hour.** The D1 and the Prague ring seize up 07:00–09:00 and 15:00–18:00. Fallback: leave Kutná Hora before 07:00 or after 10:00; the difference is 45 minutes.
